citeAs: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach (2019). Towards VQA Models That Can Read. CVPR 2019.
creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach (Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology)
description: TextVQA is a Visual Question Answering dataset containing 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reading and reasoning about text present in the images to answer. Images are sourced from Open Images v3 categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard), and each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by human annotators.
name: TextVQA
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions; 3 or more annotators agree on the most common answer for 97.9% of questions. Human accuracy on the dataset is 85.01% on validation and 86.79% on test, consistent with human accuracy on VQA 2.0 and VizWiz.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage crowdsourcing pipeline: Stage 1 — annotators flagged images without text using a forced-choice yes/no flag; Stage 2 — annotators provided questions requiring reading text in the image (instructions: "Please ensure that answering the question requires reading of the text in the image. It is OK if the answer cannot be directly copied from the text but needs to be inferred or paraphrased."); a second question with a different answer was also collected per image; Stage 3 — 10 answers were collected per question following instructions similar to VQA and VizWiz datasets. Annotators could flag questions as: no text in image, not a question, answering doesn't require reading text, or unanswerable. Questions where a majority of workers marked any flag were removed. Hand-crafted questions with known answers were used to identify and filter bad annotators.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset was intentionally collected from images containing text (from specific Open Images categories like billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard) to focus on text-reading VQA, which means it does not represent the full distribution of everyday images. The paper notes that question-only and image-only baselines achieve low accuracy (8.09% and 6.29% respectively), suggesting the dataset does not have significant biases with respect to images and questions alone. The model trained on TextVQA shows a bias toward predicting "new york" for city-related questions.
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from Open Images v3 dataset, selecting categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard). A three-stage crowdsourcing pipeline was used: (1) annotators identified and filtered out images without text, resulting in 28,408 images; (2) annotators provided 1-2 questions per image requiring reading the text to answer; (3) 10 answers were collected per question. Training and validation sets were collected from Open Images' training set; the test set from Open Images' test set.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from Open Images v3 dataset, specifically from categories that tend to contain text such as billboard, traffic sign, and whiteboard. 100 random images were sampled from each category (or all images if fewer than 100 existed), and the Rosetta OCR system was run on them to compute average OCR boxes per category, which were used as sampling weights.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: 8.9% of TextVQA questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens, which the LoRRA model cannot handle (left as future work). The OCR system fails at detecting text that is rotated, unstructured (e.g., a scribble), or partially occluded. The dataset's diverse answer space (49.2% unique majority answers) makes it difficult to use a fixed answer space. Questions were collected from sighted humans rather than visually impaired users.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images without text were filtered out in Stage 1 of the pipeline (forced-choice yes/no flag by annotators), resulting in 28,408 images from an initial pool. Noisy data from annotators was also filtered. Questions where a majority of workers marked quality flags (no text in image, not a question, answering doesn't require reading text, unanswerable) were removed. Bad annotators were identified and filtered using hand-crafted questions with known correct answers.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset addresses a critical need for visually impaired users, as studies (VizWiz) found that up to 21% of questions asked by visually impaired users on images of their surroundings involve reading and reasoning about text. TextVQA is intended to drive progress on VQA models that can assist visually impaired users in reading text in their environment.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking VQA models that can read and reason about text in images; developing assistive technology for visually impaired users (answering questions about everyday images involving text); encouraging research on text detection and recognition in unconstrained environments; studying the ability of VQA models to read and reason about text.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Rosetta OCR system was used to compute average number of OCR boxes per Open Images category, which were used as per-category weights for sampling images for the dataset.
